summary: This rare form stands beside cattle in the psalm’s list of animals. Its sense and consonants connect it with the usual Hebrew collective for flocks.

senses.definition: Psalm 8 names the sheep and oxen under human care before turning to wild animals, birds and fish. The rare sheep word functions collectively. Numbers has a similar expanded form for the livestock that need enclosures.

note: The entry key follows the rare spelling. The common word צֹאן, its Syriac equivalent and the place-name Zaanan already belong to tson. Psalm 8 has neither the usual aleph nor the normal ending. Numbers 32:24 retains the aleph in its suffixed form. The index groups the rare form with צמת, whose verb means to put an end to something.
